full_judgment:
2. Accused Khalil and Nawab Ali were tried in absentia. The accused appellant Nurul Islam filed Criminal Appeal No. 961 of 1996 before a Bench of this Court and was acquitted. The appellant filed this appeal with delay which was condoned. 

 3. The prosecution case is that, PW 5 Madhu Mia, full brother of the deceased laid information before Araihazar police-station stating that on the night following 29-10-92 at about 2-00 AM some miscreants broke open the door of the but of deceased Ali Ahmed and put on the electric light and looked for Ali Ahmed. They called out to finish Ali Ahmed as he was not in they came out of the house. Two of them stood at the door. One asked a man if he was Ali Ahmed. Other identified him and another standing by the western side of the window of the but gunned down Ali Ahmed who fell down dead on the ground. The miscreants then looted money and jewellery from the house. His brother''s wife (Bhabi) cried loud when informant, Ratan Mia, Abdul Majid, Ebadul Member, Rajab Ali and other villagers came to the place of occurrence and heard of the occurrence from his Bhabi who disclosed that she identified accused Nurul Islam, Khalil and Nawab Ali. 

 8. PW 5 the informant lodged the first information report alleging that the dacoits entered into the but of Ali Ahmed by breaking open the door and one dacoit asked for Ali Ahmed another dacoit identified Ali Ahmed who was shot to death by Nurul Islam who was assisted by the appellant Khalil and Nawab being armed with knives. It is in his further testimony that after killing Ali Ahmed the dacoits ransacked the house and decamped with money, ornaments, etc. He also stated that his Bhabi (PW 4) identified the dacoits. This witness further stated that Nurul Islam was fined for committing theft by a village salish and for that reason he killed his brother. In cross-examination this witness said that there are 7/8 houses in between his and accused’s houses and many people who resided in those houses was not cited as witnesses in the case. PW 4 Cheharunnessa, the wife of the deceased, in her testimony stated that the dacoits broke open the door and three persons entered into the house and put on the electric light. One of the dacoits wanted to know who was Ali Ahmed and one dacoit identified her husband. She further stated that accused Nurul Islam, Nawab Ali and Khalil entered into the house and they came out of the house and Nurul Islam fired through the western side window upon her husband. She further stated that accused Nawab Ali and Khalil stood in front of the kitchen. In the cross-examination she denied the suggestion put forward by the defence that her husband was killed by unknown persons. PW 6 Minara Begum, the daughter of the deceased, testified that four/five persons broke open the door and entered into the house and switched on the electric light. The persons came out of the house and they stood near the window. One of them identified Ali Ahmed to another but she shielded her father when she was kicked aside and her father was shot dead straight away. She also stated that after gun-shot her mother asked Nurul Islam what he did. She asked her mother who was Nurul Islam and her mother identified Nurul Islam to her and he was in the dock. She further stated that after killing they looted away money, ornaments and other articles. This witness in answer to a question by the court stated that she used to know Nurul Islam before hand. She again stated that as neighbor she knew Nurul Islam. This witness further said that there are 10/12 houses near the spot. People assembled at the place of occurrence when they raised hue and cry after the occurrence. PW 8, the Investigating Officer in his testimony said that he went to the place of occurrence 14 times and recorded the statements of many witnesses near about the spot. He further stated that he did not examine the local Union Parishad Member, the Chairman and the Matabbars of the locality. He stated further that he recovered empty cartridge. From the evidence of PWs 4, 5 and 6 it appears that their testimonies suffer from contradictions and discrepancies. PW 4 stated that three persons entered into the house and they went out of the house and Nurul Islam shot at her husband. She also testified that accused Nawab Ali and Khalil stood in front of the kitchen. PW 6 the daughter of the deceased testified that 4/5 persons breaking open the door entered into the but and switched on the electric light. She further stated that one of the accused kicked her and one person standing outside the but fired on her father. She also stated her mother asked Nurul Islam what he did. This witness also stated that she asked her mother who was Nurul Islam. This witness in the cross-examination stated that she used to know Nurul Islam before hand as he was their neighbor. PW 4 did not state at all in her evidence what PW 6 stated. Thus we find discrepancies in evidence of PWs 4 and 6. The story of identification of the killer as stated by the PW 6 creates a great doubt. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that alleged killer Nurul Islam was acquitted by a Bench of this Division in Criminal Appeal No. 961 of 1996. The Court did not believe the evidence led by the prosecution, moreover, this appellant has taken no part in the killing and there is hardly any evidence against the appellant to convict him. We find force in the submission of the learned Advocate when we assessed the evidence and find that the appellant is entitled to the benefit of doubt. We would set aside the order of conviction and sentence of the appellant. In the result the appeal is allowed and the order of conviction and sentence dated 27-04-96 in Sessions Case No. 1 of 1995 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge Court No. 2, Narayanganj is set aside.
